§6Perfluoromethyl§f

§aThe only coolant with a cold variant - powers reactors, PWRs, and particle accelerators!§f

Perfluoromethyl is a specialized coolant derived from oil. It has three temperature variants: §bStandard§f (§e15°C§f), §bHot§f (§e250°C§f), and §bCold§f (§e-150°C§f). It holds §e300 TU/mB§f, matching the best coolants in the mod.

§6Production§f:
§b•§f §e500mB§f Unsaturated Hydrocarbons + §e1,000mB§f Petroleum Gas + Fluorite → §e1,000mB§f Perfluoromethyl.

§6Uses§f:
§b•§f RBMK Fluid Heaters, PWR, and ICF: standard coolant at §e300 TU/mB§f.
§b•§f Particle Accelerator: requires §bCold Perfluoromethyl§f (-150°C), compressed twice.
§b•§f Control Units: standard perfluoromethyl for control units, cold variant for quantum computers.

§ePS:§f Perfluoromethyl is not consumed in normal cooling cycles - it heats up and needs to be cooled back down. But §bparticle accelerators§f consume cold perfluoromethyl constantly, even when idle. Turn off compressors when not running experiments to save power!
